title: Steller's Sea Eagle — ISO 800
subtitle: Steller's Sea Eagle photographed off Rausu, Hokkaido, at 1/1600s and ISO 800. Dark plumage against bright water and snow surfaces stresses noise reduction in distinct ways — uniform low-noise backgrounds vs. fine feather detail.

images.title: RAW
images.caption: Original RAW with no editing, shot at 1/1600s and ISO 800.

critique.text: The original RAW image shot at ISO 800 shows noticeable luminance noise, particularly in the out-of-focus background water ripples. While the shutter speed of 1/1600s froze the action well, the image lacks overall crispness and micro-contrast in the fine details of the eagle's eye, beak, and feathers. The edited versions generally do an excellent job improving upon this baseline, with Lightroom and DxO providing the most balanced and natural enhancements.

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom AI Denoise at default settings

critique.text: Lightroom's AI Denoise provides an excellent balance. It successfully eradicates the background noise from the RAW file while retaining a very natural, organic sharpness in the eagle. The feather details are enhanced without appearing artificial, making it one of the strongest edits in the set.

DxO PureRAW 6 (DeepPRIME 3) delivers an outstanding result. It provides exceptional noise reduction in the background water while restoring brilliant, natural sharpness to the eagle's beak and feathers. It completely avoids the artificial 'AI' look that Topaz sometimes introduces, ranking at the top of the group alongside Lightroom.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with sharpening on subject and noise reduction on all, with default settings

critique.text: Topaz Photo with standard settings handles the noise reduction well, providing a perfectly clean background. The sharpening on the subject is strong and effective, yielding a slightly more natural result than the Wildlife setting, though it still feels slightly over-processed compared to Lightroom or DxO.

images.title: ON1 RAW
images.caption: ON1 RAW with NoNoise and TackSharp at default settings

critique.text: ON1 RAW with both NoNoise and TackSharp applied shows a marked improvement in detail over the NoNoise-only version. The noise is well-controlled, and the eagle is noticeably sharper. However, the sharpening effect feels slightly less refined than Lightroom or DxO, appearing just a bit heavy-handed on the micro-contrast.

images.title: Topaz Wildlife
images.caption: Topaz Photo with sharpening on subject using wildlife setting, and noise reduction on all, with default settings.

critique.text: Topaz Photo using the Wildlife setting delivers extremely aggressive noise reduction and sharpening. While the background is completely clean, the sharpening on the eagle is quite heavy, leading to a slightly 'crunchy' or over-processed look in the fine feather details and edges.

images.title: ON1 RAW NoNoise only
images.caption: ON1 RAW with NoNoise only at default setting

critique.text: Compared to the original RAW, ON1's NoNoise has effectively removed the visible background grain while maintaining a natural look. However, because no additional sharpening was applied, the eagle itself lacks the crispness seen in the other processed versions, leaving the subject looking slightly soft.
